title: Promo band rehearsals and the Holy Ghost band
summary: The band rehearsed in his father's dining room, played in Mobile, and a related Holy Ghost band played Catholic parades and burials.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, they had a crack brass band and they used to practice in my daddy's dining room practice every Sunday. You couldn't get to yours, let know when the other people would be around listening to them. Not only listening, we'd come and dance. Dance to the brass band.
Oh yeah, they'd practice. They used to go to the Mobile and play for dances, the brass band. Would they buck the Excelsior over there?

Well, I don't know about bucking, but they used to play over there. Yeah. And the Excelsior had a good brass band then. I know, I heard about that. Yeah, they had a good brass band them times. My dad, he's one of the best baritone players they had on the coast. Yeah. And a lot of times you'd go to New Orleans and play with some of them New Orleans bands. He's a good baritone player.
In them days you had to be good because most every brass band you played with in them
days they put that music on. That music in front of you. That's right. And every time they practiced it they had that music right in front of you.

Even rehocers. Sometimes some of them rehocers twice a week. Probably the Holy Ghost. Every Sunday. Every Sunday. On Tuesday and Friday. The Holy Ghost brass band. Yeah. Was that a school brass band? No. We used to practice up at the Holy Ghost Hall on Tuesday and Friday. And they named the band the Holy Ghost brass band. They used to play for the parade. And at that time you see Catholic had bands for the burial and everything. You know right? Mm-hm.
